headlines.title: San Bruno Post Office robbery: Public told to check financial accounts, $150K reward issued
headlines.description: The U.S. Postal Inspection Service is offering a reward of up to $150,000 for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the person or people who stole mail from the San Bruno Post Office last week. The robbery at the post office, located at 1300 Huntington Ave., happened between 4:55 p.m. and 5:10 p.m. last Thursday, officials said. At least one person entered the post office, took four tubs of mail and assaulted a postal employee, according to officials. “If you recently visited the San Bruno Post Office or deposited mail into a collection box serviced by that office — including collection boxes in the South San Francisco area — your mail may have been affected,” San Bruno police said in a post on social media. Police said residents should monitor their financial accounts for any unauthorized activity. Those who believe their mail may have been stolen or compromised are instructed to file a report with the U.S. Postal Inspection Service (reference case No. 4750763-ROBB). Anyone with information about the robbery is encouraged to contact the U.S. Postal Inspection Service at 1-877-876-2455.

headlines.title: 5 arrested in San Francisco child predator sting
headlines.description: Editor’s note: This story was updated to reflect revised arrest numbers provided by authorities. Five people were arrested, not seven. The San Francisco Sheriff’s Office and District Attorney’s Office announced the arrests of five men following a three-day undercover operation targeting suspected child predators. The operation, conducted with the help of 10 other law enforcement agencies, took place over three days at the end of July. During the investigation, officers posed as children on several online platforms. Authorities said seven men contacted the undercover investigators seeking to meet for lewd acts. According to investigators, four of the men showed up to meet who they believed were children but were instead met by law enforcement officers. The five men arrested are from San Francisco, San Mateo, Daly City and Redwood City. The four men facing felony charges remain in custody. Sheriff Paul Miyamoto and District Attorney Brooke Jenkins urged parents to use available tools to limit their children’s interactions with strangers online and to have conversations about the dangers of online grooming. “They are very clearly exploitative in nature, very clearly not appropriate relations between an adult and a minor,” Miyamoto said. “You need to be monitoring what those conversations are. You need to be talking to your children about talking to strangers,” Jenkins said. “They think about talking to strangers in person, but we need to talk to them about the dangers of talking to strangers online.” Parents looking for resources on how to protect children online can find information through the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force at icactaskforce.org.

headlines.title: Major closures coming to Carquinez Bridge
headlines.description: Major closures are coming to the Carquinez Bridge, which connects Vallejo to the East Bay. The bridge is set for a full deck replacement. Caltrans said crews need to repave the bridge to ensure safety and smoothness. Crews will begin repairs at 6 p.m. Friday, resulting in one westbound lane closure. The repair is expected to continue until 7 p.m. Saturday. A full bridge closure will start two weeks later on Aug. 21. Lanes will reopen on Aug. 24.

headlines.title: AC/DC set to hit the stage at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara
headlines.description: AC/DC will take the stage at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara Wednesday night. Crews have been preparing the stadium for fans and band members, who are now in their 70s. While fans gear up for the concert, pop-up events are being hosted in the Bay Area. The Hard Rock Cafe at Fisherman’s Wharf in San Francisco is hosting a special pop-up store, providing fans with tour items and memorabilia that cannot be found anywhere else.

headlines.title: Deadly mass shooting near Morgan Hill: FBI joins investigation, offers $20K reward
headlines.description: The FBI has joined the investigation into last month’s deadly mass shooting at a pop-up birthday party near Morgan Hill and is offering a reward of up to $20,000 for information leading to an arrest, the Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office said Wednesday. Seven people were shot, one fatally, during the party on Saturday, July 25, at a rural property along Hale Avenue, officials said. The party, which was advertised on social media, drew hundreds of attendees. The sheriff’s office said the FBI’s involvement in the investigation will bring “significant federal resources and technical support” into play as authorities work to identify the person or persons responsible. “With hundreds of people in attendance, someone knows something,” Santa Clara County Sheriff Robert Jonsen said in a statement. “We’ve asked for the FBI’s assistance, and we are calling on our community to help identify those responsible for this heinous crime. We are grateful the FBI is stepping forward and encouraging others to do the same.” Anyone who was in the area at the time of the shooting and captured photos, videos or other forms of digital content is encouraged to upload their files via the FBI’s digital media tip line. “Those responsible for this senseless shooting should know that the FBI and our law enforcement partners at the Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office will use every available resource to identify and hold them accountable,” FBI San Francisco Special Agent in Charge Scott Schelble said in a statement. “The FBI is offering a reward of up to $20,000 because we believe someone has information that can help move this investigation forward. No piece of information is too small, and your tip could make a difference in bringing justice to the victims, their families, and the Morgan Hill community.” Anyone with additional information about the shooting is asked to call the FBI at 1‑800‑CALL‑FBI. headlines.title: Businesses in San Jose's Branham Plaza burglarized
headlines.description: At least six stores at Branham Plaza in San Jose were burglarized Monday night, according to business owners. The strip mall is located at Pearl Avenue and Branham Lane, not far from Capitol Expressway. It wasn’t immediately known what was stolen from the businesses. Crews were busy Tuesday boarding up glass doors and windows that were damaged by the vandals. Meanwhile, San Jose police were searching for who was responsible for the string of burglaries.

headlines.title: Man convicted of burning Jewish scroll at Berkeley religious study center
headlines.description: A jury has convicted a 45-year-old man of arson after he used a pocket torch to burn a Jewish religious scroll at the entrance of a Berkeley study center in February, the Alameda County District Attorney’s Office said. Jurors found David William Denton guilty of arson in connection with the Feb. 6 blaze at a religious study center on Bancroft Way, where authorities said he vandalized and set fire to a mezuzah scroll attached to a doorway. The fire damaged the religious item, prosecutors said Tuesday. Following the verdict, a judge ordered Denton into custody pending sentencing. He faces a maximum sentence of three years in state prison and will be required to register as an arson offender if sentenced, prosecutors said. “Targeting and burning a sacred religious symbol is an act that can cause harm far beyond the physical damage itself,” District Attorney Ursula Jones Dickson said in a statement. “People of every faith should be able to practice their religion and gather in their communities without fear of intimidation.” Denton will be sentenced on Sept. 3.

headlines.title: Walnut Creek house fire leaves 1 person injured, 2 dogs dead
headlines.description: Fire crews with the Contra Costa County Fire Protection District fought a two-alarm house fire in Walnut Creek on Tuesday afternoon that injured one person and killed two dogs. The call came in at 3:39 p.m. reporting a fire in a single-family residence in the 700 block of Woodwind Place in Walnut Creek, according to Con Fire. Crews arrived to find visible flames and smoke and eventually a second alarm was called on the blaze. The fire was knocked down by 4:30 p.m., but as of 5:30 p.m., firefighters were still at the scene handling hot spots and other issues, Con Fire said. One person was transported to the hospital for smoke inhalation, according to Con Fire, but it is unclear if they were a resident of the home or a neighbor. Two dogs perished in the fire. The cause of the fire is still under investigation.

headlines.title: SFMTA announces more Muni service on popular routes
headlines.description: The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency will add more service on key routes starting in a few weeks as more people return to school and work. “These changes will bring immediate improvements to thousands of riders traveling key corridors to school and to work,” SFMTA Director of Transportation Julie Kirschbaum said in a statement, as the agency held its Board of Directors meeting on Tuesday. For students, there will be extra afternoon buses along school routes to help transport them. A stop will be added for the 28R-19th Avenue Rapid bus at Eucalyptus Drive, which SFMTA expects students at Lowell High School to use. “I won’t have to worry about missing the 28 bus and getting to school late anymore because there’s always going to be another one soon,” said Woody Szydlik, a Lowell High School student, in a statement from an SFMTA release. Students and educators traveling from Visitacion Valley to Francisco Middle School will have a direct bus route, eliminating a transfer that was previously required on the 8AX-Bayshore Express bus. SFMTA is also going to increase the frequency of trips for the N-Judah train, which can often get packed during commute hours. Trips will increase from every 10 minutes to every nine minutes during peak hours, a change that could see a 10% increase in space for passengers on the trains, according to Kirschbaum. There will be a higher frequency of buses on the 1-California route, also increasing trips from 10 minutes to nine minutes. Buses on this route in the Presidio and downtown areas should arrive every four to five minutes. The 5R-Fulton Rapid route will have larger buses. Capacity increases will also be made during the busiest times on the 22-Fillmore, 29-Sunset, 38R-Geary Rapid, and 49-Van Ness/Mission. “For the majority of our customers, these changes are not going to make it more complex to navigate the system,” Kirschbaum said at the meeting. “There’s not a lot of learning to do, but we do think customers will see some small but meaningful benefits to their travel.” The changes, Kirschbaum said, are able to happen without additional costs to the agency. SFMTA has identified $250 million in cost savings by reducing redundant service options and adjusting system schedules to boost efficiency. “Our staff is looking at this entire optimization and service puzzle and making smart choices to keep up with our changing conditions,” said Kirschbaum. An overview of the service changes can be found at sfmta.com. The page will be updated Wednesday with more details on the changes.

headlines.title: Man killed in targeted Novato shooting; police search for suspect
headlines.description: A 31-year-old man was killed in what police believe was a targeted, gang-related shooting Tuesday morning, prompting a search for the suspect. Novato police responded to reports of a shooting on Alameda del Prado. Arriving officers found the man suffering from a life-threatening gunshot wound, according to the Novato Police Department. Medics provided emergency care at the scene before transporting him in critical condition to a local hospital, where he later died from his injuries. The suspect fled the scene on foot toward Calle Arboleda before officers arrived. Preliminary investigations indicate the shooting was a targeted attack. Novato police officers, detectives, and crime scene investigators are actively working to locate the suspect and are asking for the community’s assistance. The suspect is described as a Latin man, approximately 5 feet, 6 inches tall. He was last seen fleeing on foot in the area of Calle Arboleda and Alameda del Prado wearing dark pants, a gray hooded sweatshirt, and a black ski mask. Authorities warn the public not to approach the suspect. Anyone who spots him is urged to call 911 immediately. Anyone with information regarding the case or relevant security camera footage is asked to contact the NPD at 415-897-4361 or email crimetips@novato.gov to remain anonymous. Reference case number NP26-2062.

headlines.title: Outside Lands festival brings music, food to Golden Gate Park
headlines.description: It’s that time of year again as the annual Outside Lands festival takes over Golden Gate Park for a weekend of music and food. The three-day festival kicks off Friday, featuring 90 bands and an expected attendance of more than 200,000 fans across the weekend. This year’s headlining acts include Charli XCX, The Strokes, Rüfüs Du Sol and PinkPantheress. NBC’s Christie Smith is providing a closer look at what attendees can expect on the festival grounds. While the music is the main draw, the food and drink options are a close second. Festivalgoers will have the option of sampling dishes from 100 Bay Area restaurants, which includes 18 new restaurants this year. The culinary lineup features notable establishments such as Nobu, Brenda’s Soul Food, and the Michelin-starred Angler. Tanya Kollar serves as the food curator for Outside Lands, overseeing the massive operation. In a preview of the festival’s dining experience, Kollar was asked to detail her selection process and explain what makes the food at Outside Lands unique compared to other music festivals. She also weighed in on which two dishes stand out the most this year and offered recommendations on what fans should get to drink.

headlines.title: Gann Fire burns more than 7,000 acres in Calaveras County
headlines.description: Mandatory evacuation orders and warnings remain in effect in Calaveras County as the Gann Fire continues to threaten homes east of Stockton. The wildfire, which started Tuesday evening, has grown to more than 7,000 acres. At least one home has been destroyed by the fire, and while there is no official count of damaged structures, NBC Bay Area crews have observed additional homes destroyed. The growing fire danger in Northern California comes as large wildfires continue burning out of control in Oregon and Washington state. NBC Bay Area’s Kris Sanchez has the full report in the video above.
